analysis: The two supplied units are BASE-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1645-2464). The PR changes to this file are documentation-only (date stamp, and prose about serial-prefill Gemma 4 pipeline default lane width, with additions near head lines 126-129, 3048, 3100, 4483-4538, 4901-4927). The patch excerpt is truncated, and the changed regions do not overlap the supplied base units, so there is no changed code behavior visible in these units. I examined the base text for security-relevant claims: deadline admission (prefill_deadline_mode, DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment.permitsQualification rejecting DARKBLOOM_* overrides), MTP typical acceptance (documented as approximate, not distribution-exact; exact opt-out), sampling defaults, constrained JSON decoding and tool-call forced-mode validation. None of these are modified here, and none alter coordinator/provider trust boundaries, key custody (A-003), attestation (TB-009/TB-011), or the prefix-cache threat T-041 (SSD cache, HMAC names, TTL). Documentation claims about the Gemma pipeline lane default are not verifiable from the supplied evidence: the new anchor [Gemma pipeline lanes] and the head-side content (4505-4538, 4901-4927) were not in the supplied units, so any claim about changed default lane width and its memory or admission impact belongs to a pass that sees the head text. No threat-model assumption appears invalidated by the visible content. Remaining question for integration: whether the new Gemma pipeline default (cluster/pipeline mode, multi-lane serving) introduces a new trust boundary or cross-node plaintext exposure that the threat model should capture; this cannot be judged from these units.
